description: Does the battery do what the model assumes: commanded against actual power, clamped power, SOC tracking and round-trip efficiency (battery-optimizer service metrics; KPIs of docs/components/battery-model.md).

panels.title: Actuator state (guard, readiness and inputs: Battery optimizer shadow service)
Actuation mode
panels.description: dry_run computes and records writes, live sends them (ADR-0007). In shadow there is no actuator, so this panel has no data.

panels.title: In control
panels.description: 1 while the actuator owns the Omnibattery controls.

panels.title: Kill switch
panels.description: The owner's kill switch (read only). ON means nothing is written.

panels.title: Last tick applied
panels.description: 1 when the last tick applied the plan's intent (no guard reason active).

panels.title: Active guard reasons
panels.description: Number of guard reasons active at the last tick (actuator_guard_reason == 1).

panels.title: Write alert
panels.description: 1 while writes fail (fell back to safe idle, or even that failed).

panels.title: Battery power: commanded, final plan and actual (W, + charge, - discharge)
panels.description: All three use the service's sign: + charge, - discharge. Final plan: slot_battery_power_watts{plan=final}, the intent frozen at the slot open (+ charge). Actual: actuator_observed_battery_power_watts, the measured battery AC power; the service already negates Home Assistant's sensor.venus_ac_power (+ while discharging), so + is charge here. Commanded is derived from the actuator's request, which is not itself a battery power: in a charge slot the PD target is a grid-IMPORT setpoint (>= 0) equal to house load + planned charge, so charge = PD target - house load (floored at 0); in a discharge slot the request is the system discharge cap, drawn as - cap (a ceiling: the battery delivers less when the house needs less); idle is 0. The house load is the estimate at the scrape (grid - battery power), not at the tick, so the charge level is approximate. Commanded has data in dry_run and live only.

panels.title: PD grid-import target: requested and observed (W, import, never negative)
panels.description: The raw actuator request. Requested: actuator_desired_pd_target_watts. Observed: actuator_observed_pd_target_watts, the number as Home Assistant reports it. They should be equal after a write; a difference is a write that did not land or an entity that cuts the value. This is a grid-import setpoint (house load + charge power when charging, a small margin when discharging, the neutral value when idle), not a battery power: do not compare it with the power panel above. The estimated house load (grid - battery AC power) is shown for reference.

panels.title: System discharge cap requested (W)
panels.description: actuator_desired_max_discharge_watts: the system discharge cap the actuator asked for. It exists only in discharge slots (a gap elsewhere, never a 0).

panels.title: Clamped power (W)
panels.description: actuator_clamped_watts: the planned battery power the last tick could not request, because the PD target or the discharge cap was cut by the import cap or the entity's own maximum. A magnitude, not signed; 0 means nothing was cut. dry_run and live only.

panels.title: Energy clipped by the replay (kWh, rolling 24 h)
panels.description: increase(shadow_clipped_energy_kwh_total[1d]): requested energy the shadow replay had to clip (SOC window, power, import ceiling, no export). This is the replay's clipping, not the real battery's.

panels.title: Final plan energy not delivered (kWh, rolling 24 h)
panels.description: Planned minus actual AC battery energy over the last 24 h, by direction: increase(shadow_planned_energy_kwh_total) - increase(shadow_actual_battery_energy_kwh_total). Positive: the final plan asked for more than the battery moved. Negative: it moved more than planned. Slot-level detail is in Battery: plan vs actual.

panels.title: State of charge: final plan target and actual (%)
panels.description: Final plan: the planned SOC at the END of the slot in progress (slot_soc_target_ratio{plan=final}), stepping every 15 minutes. Actual: sensor.venus_battery_soc. Inside a slot the two are not comparable point by point; the error panel compares them at the slot boundary.

panels.title: SOC error at the slot boundary (actual - final plan target, points)
panels.description: In the first 2 minutes of each quarter hour: the measured SOC minus the SOC the final plan targeted for the end of the slot that just closed (the plan value 15 minutes earlier). Positive: more charged than planned. Points only, one cluster per slot. Offline equivalent: soc.<plan>.mae_frac and bias_frac of hack/day_ahead_kpis.py.

panels.title: SOC error MAE (24 h, points)
panels.description: Mean of |actual - final plan target| at the slot boundaries over the last 24 h.

panels.title: SOC error bias (24 h, points)
panels.description: Mean of (actual - final plan target) at the slot boundaries over the last 24 h. Positive: the battery ends slots more charged than planned.

panels.title: Battery AC energy: charge and discharge per day (kWh, rolling 24 h)
panels.description: shadow_actual_battery_energy_kwh_total{direction}: the AC energy the battery actually moved, increase over 24 h, both directions positive.

panels.title: Discharge / charge energy ratio and RTE estimate (rolling 24 h)
panels.description: Discharge/charge ratio: AC energy out over AC energy in over the last 24 h. It is NOT the round-trip efficiency unless the SOC is the same at both ends of the window: a net discharge of stored energy pushes it above the true RTE, a net charge below it (above 1 means the battery gave back energy stored earlier). RTE estimate: the same ratio, drawn only while the measured SOC changed by 3 points or less over the window, which bounds the stored-energy error at a few percent of a typical day's charge; the line has gaps whenever the condition fails. Standby draw is inside both. No battery capacity is assumed, so no SOC correction is attempted. Offline: battery.actual.discharge_kwh / charge_kwh over a window that starts and ends at the same SOC.

panels.title: SOC change over the same 24 h (points)
panels.description: Measured SOC now minus SOC 24 h earlier, the stored-energy term the ratio panel ignores: 0 means the ratio is a clean efficiency estimate; each point is about 1% of the usable capacity.

panels.title: Discharge margin (W)
panels.description: actuation.discharge_margin_w as the service reports it: the grid import kept while discharging.

panels.title: Margin can be lowered
panels.description: State of the BatteryMarginCanBeLowered alert (7 clean days at the current margin: at most 7 Wh exported, lowest 0.1% of discharge-time grid samples at 25 W or more, over 50000 samples). The change is manual: lower actuation.discharge_margin_w by 25 W.

panels.title: Grid export while discharging (Wh and s, rolling 24 h)
panels.description: Left axis: energy the Shelly's device-integrated returned-energy counter recorded in the last 24 h (the BatteryGridExport source; about 1 Wh/day expected at 100 W, alerts above 5 Wh). Right axis: seconds with grid power below 0 W while discharging, from the service's 2 s samples (battery_optimizer_actuator_export_seconds_total). Neither is counted while Home Assistant is down.

panels.title: Lowest 0.1% of discharge-time grid power (W, rolling 7 d)
panels.description: histogram_quantile(0.001) of battery_optimizer_actuator_discharge_grid_watts over 7 days: the grid power (+ import) that 99.9% of the discharge-time samples stay above, by measured battery discharge power band, and all bands together (the alert's input). The alert needs it at 25 W or more. Bucket resolution is 25 W below 100 W, so read it as a bucket bound.

panels.title: Extra discharge above plan (kWh)
panels.description: Energy the value rule discharged above the planned cap while engaged, over the dashboard time range (actuator_load_following_extra_kwh_total{rule="storage_value"}; counters restart with the pod, increase() handles it).

panels.title: Value added (EUR)
panels.description: (price - wear - value of keeping) x extra kWh of the value rule, over the time range: what discharging now earned over keeping the energy, in the planner's units (actuator_load_following_extra_value_eur_total).

panels.title: Mean spread (EUR/kWh)
panels.description: Value added / extra kWh over the time range: the average price advantage of the extra discharge.

panels.title: Extra by the plan-SOC fallback (kWh)
panels.description: Energy above the planned cap while the plan-SOC rule decided (spread under the margin, or no value in the plan), over the time range.

panels.title: Slot price against the value of keeping (EUR/kWh)
panels.description: The value rule engages in a discharge slot while price >= value of keeping + wear (0.01) + margin (0.005): the dashed line.

panels.title: Discharge: cap, house load and battery (W)
panels.description: Discharge cap written (raised to 2500 W while load-following is engaged), the house load and the measured battery discharge. Engaged: 0 off, 1 plan-SOC rule, 2 value rule (right axis).
